clue.text: Wakefield vicar had a way with him which Ophelia warned Laertes against

parts.note: Dr Primrose is the title character of Goldsmith's novel The Vicar of Wakefield
a path is a way or track

explanation.surface: A country clergyman sets off down a road that a Shakespearean heroine cautioned her brother to avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, Ophelia tells Laertes not to preach virtue while himself treading 'the primrose path of dalliance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia's phrase names the easy road of pleasure that leads to ruin, which she urges her brother to shun.

clue.text: Love bird led by Thomas the author

definitions.text: Love bird led by Thomas the author

parts.words: Love bird led by Thomas the author
parts.note: the novelist's full name is Thomas Love followed by the name of a showy bird with a fanned tail, so the clue spells out his name piece by piece

explanation.definitionFit: The English satirist who wrote Nightmare Abbey bore the forenames Thomas Love and a surname that is also a gaudy bird.

clue.text: Caught in terrible ruin we thus bring on ourselves

indicators.note: the letter for caught is placed inside the rearranged letters
terrible signals that the letters of ruin are wrecked and reordered

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Being caught up in a dreadful collapse is the sort of thing we bring upon ourselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we thus' is a link here: the definition is what we do to ourselves. 'terrible' scrambles the ruin and 'in' sets the cricket C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost or penalty is to bring it upon yourself through your own actions.

clue.text: Recall to arms strangely ever stirs him

definitions.text: Recall to arms strangely ever stirs him

indicators.note: strangely tells the solver that the letters of the two following words appear in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A summons back to military duty oddly always rouses a former soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a recall to arms is exactly what rouses a man held in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservist is a former serviceman kept on a list to be recalled to the forces in an emergency.

clue.text: This wide boy upset the bigwigs

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the word is turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: VIPs, very important persons, are bigwigs

explanation.surface: A small-time crook has thrown important people into disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wide boy' is British slang for a flashy petty dealer in black-market goods, the kind found after the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms are British slang for a flashy, shady trader who lives by petty dodges.

clue.text: Bagheera for instance endlessly performing in the Temple

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the big cat's name is cut off

parts.note: Bagheera is the black panther in Kipling's The Jungle Book
a performer is on, that is on stage

explanation.surface: A big cat from Kipling keeps on performing inside a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the R from PANTHER, leaving PANTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is a temple dedicated to all the gods, like the one in Rome.

clue.text: Work out the origins of such elements?

definitions.meaning: to find where something came from, as in following a family line
the question invites the solver to supply the word that precedes elements in the term for tiny essential minerals

explanation.definitionFit: To trace something is to track it back to its source; minute quantities in the body are called trace elements.

clue.text: Foucault's. swinger, proof of world revolution

definitions.text: Foucault's. swinger, proof of world revolution

parts.words: Foucault's. swinger, proof of world revolution
parts.note: the French physicist hung a heavy bob on a long wire in Paris, and the slow turning of its swing plane proved that the earth spins; world revolution suggests political upheaval instead

explanation.definitionFit: Foucault's swinging weight on a wire demonstrated the rotation of the earth in 1851.

clue.text: Goodfellow upset river bird — a stupid mistake

parts.note: a saint is a good fellow, abbreviated ST

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the letters are read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Puck, alias Robin Goodfellow, capsizes a waterbird in a foolish blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodfellow' (good fellow) is a saint, ST; 'upset' turns R + EMU into UMER. STUMER is old British slang for a dud cheque or a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for a worthless cheque, a dud, came to mean any flop or blunder.

clue.text: Approach one takes on becoming king

definitions.meaning: the act of drawing near, an archaic sense of the word
the step a new monarch takes when succeeding to the crown

explanation.definitionFit: Accession can mean an approach or coming near, and the act of a monarch coming to the throne.

clue.text: Concerning participation in an enterprise

indicators.note: the answer takes part in the run of letters across these words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: A remark about joining a business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Anent is an old Scottish word meaning about or regarding.

clue.text: Clockwork model system makes journey's end after error corrected

indicators.note: after places the final letter behind the rearranged letters
a mistake corrected is put right, so its letters are rearranged
the end of the word journey is its final letter

explanation.surface: A clockwork device arrives at the end of its trip after a mistake has been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrected' rearranges ERROR to ORRER; 'end' of journey gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system showing planets in motion.

clue.text: Principal Benedictine monk in the tribal domain

parts.note: chief means principal or main
Dom is the title given to a Benedictine monk

explanation.surface: The head of a monastery presides over territory belonging to a tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiefdom is the territory or rule of a tribal leader.

clue.text: The water spirit that is going after seaweed

indicators.note: going after places the abbreviation behind the seaweed

parts.note: kelp is a large brown seaweed
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A water spirit chases seaweed through the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: A kelpie is a Scottish water spirit that takes the form of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish folklore a shape-shifting horse demon haunting lochs and rivers bears this name.

clue.text: Means to check drift of directors led by the general

indicators.note: in a down clue led by means the general comes first, above the directors

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Company directors take orders from the general.
explanation.definitionFit: A leeboard is a plank lowered on the side of a sailing barge to stop it slipping sideways.

clue.text: Such status Caligula proposed for his horse

definitions.text: Such status Caligula proposed for his horse

parts.words: Such status Caligula proposed for his horse
parts.note: the Roman emperor is said to have planned to make his favourite horse Incitatus one of the two chief magistrates of Rome

explanation.definitionFit: Caligula reportedly intended to appoint his horse to Rome's highest elected magistracy.

clue.text: Awareness of one in so many words

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one within the group of words

parts.note: a sentence is a set number of words
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Knowing that one person stands out among so much verbiage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel and perceive, that is, consciousness.

clue.text: Have to go on, battered by hail storm — that's rough

indicators.note: battered means the letters are knocked about and reshaped

explanation.surface: A traveller presses on through a hailstorm in rough weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' rearranges GO ON + HAIL; 'storm' adds to the weather picture. A rough is a hooligan, a violent lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a rowdy thug, the same sort of lout as a hoodlum.

clue.text: The little matter of a small boy's slogan when standing for Parliament

parts.note: a candidate's slogan urges voters to elect him
Ron is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: A young lad's campaign poster for a seat in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The slogan reads 'Elect Ron'. 'The little matter' is a joke: the particle is a tiny bit of matter.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle is one of the smallest units of matter.

clue.text: Manager supports printers' measure to do relief work

indicators.note: in a down clue supports places the manager below the measure, holding it up

parts.note: an em is a unit of measure in printing
a boss is a manager

explanation.surface: A manager backs printing staff in a charitable project.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to carve or stamp a design in raised relief.

clue.text: Are some Swiss bankers so sententious?

definitions.text: Are some Swiss bankers so sententious?

parts.words: Are some Swiss bankers so sententious?
parts.note: Zurich financiers are nicknamed after small bearded garden goblins, so the adjective sounds as if it describes them, while really meaning full of pithy maxims

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means given to aphorisms and pithy sayings, which suits the solemn speech of figures nicknamed after goblins.

clue.text: State University came across what Gitche Manito smoked

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, an American state
met means came across or encountered

explanation.surface: A state university stumbled upon a spirit's pipe in Longfellow's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Gitche Manito, the Great Spirit in Longfellow's Hiawatha, smokes a peace pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A calumet is the ceremonial tobacco pipe of North American peoples, the pipe of peace.

clue.text: Vegetable — cook or boil with heads of cauliflowers and carrots

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so the letters are mixed
the heads of the two vegetables are their first letters

explanation.surface: Instructions to prepare a green with cauliflower and carrots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' rearranges OR BOIL plus the C and C from 'heads of'.
explanation.definitionFit: This green relative of the cabbage is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Short sketch that amounted to nothing

parts.note: came, as in came to a sum, means amounted
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A brief play that added up to very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amounted to' = came to; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a brief vivid literary portrait or a short dramatic scene.

clue.text: Ancient firearm

definitions.meaning: an ensign or standard-bearer, the rank of Shakespeare's braggart in Henry IV and Henry V

explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Pistol is the swaggering ensign in Shakespeare's Henry plays, and the word also names a handgun.

clue.text: Metaphor Ham dispenses with possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters left over are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ham actor gives up figurative language.
explanation.walkthrough: Take HAM from METAPHOR ('dispenses with') and 'possibly' rearranges the remaining ETPOR. The whole clue defines too: a metaphor is one figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphor is an example of a figure of speech, one kind among many.

clue.text: Charitable function has the sound of doom

indicators.note: has the sound of signals a word that is spoken like another

parts.note: fate means doom

explanation.surface: The charity bazaar sounds doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: A fete is a British outdoor fundraising fair with stalls and games.
explanation.definitionFit: A village fair held to raise money for charity is a common British example.

clue.text: To wit, the spirit of football players en masse

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely or to wit
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Namely, the team spirit of footballers gathered together.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is football here: a scrum is the packed formation of forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the forwards bind together in a tight pushing pack.

clue.text: Immature Othello retires here off-stage

parts.note: green means immature or inexperienced

indicators.note: retires means the word goes back, reading right to left

parts.note: Othello is the Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: An inexperienced actor playing Othello withdraws to the lounge behind the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors relax in this backstage lounge when not performing.

clue.text: High spot where move appears out of tune perhaps with the others

indicators.note: out of signals the letters break out of their order

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A mountaineering party moves on out of step with the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' rearranges MOVE, TUNE and REST (the others).
explanation.definitionFit: This Himalayan peak is the highest point on the earth.
